fields.value: Read a training metric run's history in constant memory

## Problem

Reading a long run's retained per-update metrics through the normal reader loads the whole cumulative manifest. On manabot's width-64 frontier run (59718fe34945, \~1,744 updates), a 1.3–1.4 GB manifest expanded to about 14 GB RSS in the reader. Reports and diagnostics over long runs therefore need a large machine or can't run at all.

manabot MTG-281 (abandoned 2026-11-12) worked around this with a manabot-side script that reads one raw block header and its selected arrays at a time, keeping Etude's block selection and CRC checks. That code is preserved at loopflowstudio/manabot commit 3b3c8a89190fec9e2c973736042e848a03a1f308 (ref `archive/mtg-281-collection-growth`), file `scripts/measure_collection_growth.py`, with tests in `tests/infra/test_collection_growth_capture.py`. Etude is ours, so the fix belongs here as a supported reader, not as a manabot workaround.

## Outcome

Etude can stream a metric run's history update by update (or block by block) with peak memory bounded by one block plus the selected metrics, not by run length. It keeps the existing semantics: winning update/attempt selection, supersession, sparse rows, CRC/digest validation, and failure on missing or corrupt selected evidence. Existing readers either use it or stay correct.

Show it on a fixture with many blocks: peak traced/RSS memory stays flat as block count grows, while the current reader grows.

## Constraints

* EXP-46 (keep training metric logging cheap for long runs and many metric names) owns the write side and manifest growth. Don't duplicate it; build on whatever it lands, and coordinate if they touch the same reader code.
* Never induce artificial load; use controlled fixtures.
* Don't rewrite retained run data.
